g1.label: 1 — what a normal working ___ looks like
g1.why: "A working day" is the fixed phrase for the hours people spend at work.

g2.label: 2 — a whole term of ___
g2.why: A school term is made up of lessons.

g3.label: 3 — invited to an ___
g3.why: A company invites you to an interview — a meeting where they ask you questions.

g4.label: 4 — the work is usually ___
g4.why: Unpaid means you get no money for it, which is normal for school placements.

g5.label: 5 — answer the ___
g5.why: "Answer the phone" is the set phrase for taking a call.

g6.label: 6 — whether you ___ the noise
g6.why: Enjoy fits a feeling about the noise and the people; "employ" means to give somebody a job.

g7.label: 7 — you write a ___
g7.why: A report describes what you did and learned during the placement.

g8.label: 8 — never want to ___ the experience
g8.why: To repeat something is to do it again.

g1.label: 1 — where the office ___
g1.why: In an indirect question the word order is normal: subject ("the office") before the verb.

g2.label: 2 — what time the shop ___
g2.why: The auxiliary "does" disappears in an indirect question and the -s stays on the verb.

g3.label: 3 — I’d like to know ___ you offer placements
g3.why: A yes/no question becomes "whether" or "if" — never "that".

g4.label: 4 — how much a ticket ___
g4.why: No "does" after "how much" here: the subject is followed directly by "costs".

g5.label: 5 — she asked me ___ I had experience

g6.label: 6 — where I ___ find the manager
g6.why: Normal word order: "where I can find", not "where can I find".

g7.label: 7 — I wonder ___ the interview will take
g7.why: Time is measured with "how long"; "how far" is distance and "how much" is quantity.

g8.label: 8 — why the train ___ late
g8.why: After "why the train" the verb comes straight after the subject, with no inversion.

g1.label: 1 — you’ve sent your application, ___?
g1.why: A positive sentence takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary — here "have".

g2.label: 2 — she isn’t coming, ___?
g2.why: A negative sentence takes a positive tag.

g3.label: 3 — let’s ask the manager, ___?
g3.why: Sentences starting with "Let’s" always take "shall we".

g4.label: 4 — you’ll call me tomorrow, ___?
g4.why: The auxiliary in the tag matches "will", so the negative form is "won’t you".

g5.label: 5 — nobody told you, ___?
g5.why: "Nobody" is already negative, so the tag is positive — and it takes "they".

g6.label: 6 — I have to ___ the form (phrasal verb)
g6.why: You fill in a form — from the India phrasal verbs unit.

g7.label: 7 — the woman ___ interviewed me (relative pronoun)
g7.why: "Who" is the relative pronoun for people — from the Famous & Hollywood unit.

g8.label: 8 — there’s a bus at eight, ___?
g8.why: After "there is" the tag keeps "there" as the subject.
